**DynaLM 0.6.0.** Faster CPU generation on x86-64, speculative decoding with EAGLE-3 draft heads, and mixture-of-experts models larger than RAM.

## Faster on x86-64 CPUs

On a 4-core AMD EPYC (Zen 2, AVX2), against llama.cpp's `llama-server` on the same Q4_K_M files, one user, time per output token:

| Model | DynaLM | llama.cpp | DynaLM vs llama.cpp |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-4B with EAGLE-3 | 90.7 ms | 127.6 ms | **1.41×** |
| Qwen3-8B with EAGLE-3 | 154.2 ms | 206.9 ms | **1.34×** |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | 39.2 ms | 45.0 ms | **1.15×** |
| Qwen3-4B | 93.7 ms | 109.5 ms | **1.17×** |
| Qwen3-8B | 160.5 ms | 172.3 ms | **1.07×** |

- **New AVX2 kernels** in DynaCore (`--mode exact`): 1.29–1.32× faster per token than 0.5.0. Accuracy stays within DynaLM's rule (Qwen2.5-1.5B perplexity +0.20%, Qwen3-4B +0.01% against fp32).
- **EAGLE-3 speculative decoding** (`--spec-eagle DIR`): a small head trained for the model drafts up to `--spec-k` tokens, and the model checks them all in one pass. The output is the same as without it.

```sh
dynalm run qwen3:4b --mode exact --spec-eagle ~/Qwen3-4B_eagle3
```

Heads: [AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3](https://huggingface.co/AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3) (and the Qwen3-8B head, converted to `model.safetensors`).

Details and raw data: [docs/perf/x86-zen2-2026-11.md](https://github.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/blob/v0.6.0/docs/perf/x86-zen2-2026-11.md).

## Mixture-of-experts models larger than RAM

- `--experts-from-disk`: the experts are read from the model file into a RAM cache when the router picks them (`--expert-cache SIZE`), and the next layer's experts are read ahead. The output is identical to the whole model held in RAM.
- `--prompt-cache DIR`: prompts' KV cache is kept as files and reused, also after a restart.
- Split GGUF models (`NAME-00001-of-0000N.gguf`) load as one model.

## Also

- `--spec-k` now applies to `--spec-eagle` in `benchmark` and `serve`.
- [docs/benchmarks.md](https://github.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/blob/v0.6.0/docs/benchmarks.md) lists all current results: Apple M4 Pro CPU (1.53× llama.cpp, 2.7–2.9× less memory), Metal, and AMD EPYC.

Full list: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/blob/v0.6.0/CHANGELOG.md).
